rationale.statement: Rice is the traditional and best-suited crop for the Cauvery delta zone with adequate water availability from both rainfall and canal irrigation.
The projected near-normal rainfall supports standard transplanting schedules and water management practices.
Blackgram is an excellent rotation crop with rice, fixing nitrogen and requiring only 300-350mm water. It can be cultivated as a second crop after rice harvest.
Sesame performs well in the delta zone as a rainfed crop and offers good market returns with relatively low water requirements.

irrigation_guidance.statement: With near-normal rainfall expected, follow standard irrigation scheduling. Ensure canal water allocation is confirmed before transplanting.
Adopt alternate wetting and drying (AWD) technique to save 15-20% irrigation water without yield penalty.

warnings: Monitor northeast monsoon onset timing for Samba rice transplanting decisions.

P-tnj00001.text: Rice (Paddy) in Cauvery Delta: The delta zone is ideally suited for rice cultivation with assured irrigation from the Cauvery river system and northeast monsoon rainfall. Water requirement: 1200-1400mm for transplanted rice. Recommended varieties: CO 51, ADT 53, BPT 5204 (Samba Mahsuri). Samba season transplanting: August-September. Kuruvai season: June-July.
P-tnj00001.doc_title: Rice Production Technology for Tamil Nadu

P-tnj00002.text: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) in Rice: AWD technique saves 15-25% irrigation water compared to continuous flooding without significant yield reduction. The field is allowed to dry until hairline cracks appear before re-irrigation. This technique also reduces methane emissions by 30-40%. Suitable for areas with reliable water access but conservation goals.
P-tnj00002.doc_title: Water Saving Technologies in Rice Cultivation

P-tnj00003.text: Blackgram (Urad) as Rice Fallow Crop: Blackgram is the most popular rice fallow crop in the Cauvery delta, utilizing residual soil moisture. Water requirement: 300-350mm. Duration: 70-80 days. It fixes 40-50 kg N/ha, benefiting subsequent rice crop. Recommended varieties: VBN 8, ADT 5. Sowing: immediately after rice harvest in January-February.
P-tnj00003.doc_title: Pulse Crops for Rice-Based Cropping Systems
P-tnj00003.publishing_body: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research

P-tnj00005.text: Cropping System Recommendations for Cauvery Delta Zone: The predominant cropping system is Rice-Rice-Pulse. In years with adequate northeast monsoon (>500mm during Oct-Dec), the Samba rice season can be extended. Canal water release schedule should be confirmed before nursery preparation. Rice varieties with shorter duration (ADT 43, 100-105 days) are recommended when planting is delayed beyond August.
P-tnj00005.doc_title: Agro-Climatic Zone Crop Planning Guide - Tamil Nadu

P-tnj00004.text: Sesame in Delta Zone: Sesame (Gingelly) is a traditional oilseed crop of the delta zone, cultivated as a rainfed crop during Kharif. Water requirement: 350-400mm. Short duration (85-90 days). Good market demand and price stability. Recommended varieties: TMV 7, SVPR 1. Sowing: June-July.
